bullets.title: The Technology Brothers Have Silicon Valley in Their Thrall. Now They’re Coming for You
bullets.creator: Julia Black
bullets.note: (_Vanity Fair_). Do you think it’s too crowded to do X, whatever you might be considering? Well, think again, as there is always room if you aim to be the _only_ and not simply the best. Owning a category of one, and being first mover, gives you a tremendous margin of safety. This is a fun read full of lessons. I suggest pairing it with [this _WSJ_ profile of the _Acquired_ gents](https://www.wsj.com/business/media/acquired-podcast-tech-business-history-strategy-90e73603?gaa_at=eafs&gaa_n=AWEtsqfyMyVux0j0RpNsepCHSNMkVYraTPoRvYpHY-oSiArOwLF7eDxEFM25w0wTZhg%3D&gaa_sig=2PrGkhQj6yt-_CpEJbVKFzbqVAPBNX0IRN_A6OHHRTf9wopqF6VVCrYGDEbUrQSslvYGbgfiLtN_-NtJ4jsM9g%3D%3D&gaa_ts=69618493) and how they carved out a spectacular niche (a big one!) in the saturated podcast ecosystem.

bullets.note: I’ve been getting a lot of questions about exogenous ketones. KETOSPIKE, formulated by Dominic D’Agostino, Ph.D., and Csilla Ari D’Agostino, Ph.D., has become my default, which I use a handful of times per week while on a ketogenic or extremely low-carb diet. I’ll mix this into coffee with a few tablespoons of cream, and I get a mild but noticeable cognitive boost for 2–3 hours.

bullets.title: This is a weird comparison, but Zcash reminds me a lot of BitTorrent…
bullets.creator: Haseeb Qureshi
bullets.note:
. I think the nature of privacy, and how much we value it, will change fundamentally in the next 2–3 years, as the realities of being fully exposed become more obvious. For several years, I’ve been tracking privacy-reclaiming technologies, and this is one that I’m paying attention to.  
​  
How would you like your online purchases, precise physical location, voting and dating preferences, health or health-adjacent information (e.g., wearables), and more to be correlated and made public? What if insurers and potential employers could purchase this information, even if done indirectly to skirt regulation? What if script kiddies worldwide could scrape most of it from publicly available data and piece it together with AI in an afternoon? What if they could also ingest all of your social media posts at the same time? This is a lot closer than people realize. In fact, most of it’s already here.  
​  
There are an estimated 4,000+ data brokers in the US alone. They already offer precise geolocation, political preferences, demographic details, real-time tracking, and [even military status or employment](https://techpolicy.sanford.duke.edu/wp-content/uploads/2021/08/Data-Brokers-and-Sensitive-Data-on-US-Individuals-Sherman-2021.pdf?utm_source=chatgpt.com). Major data brokers may have ~1,500 data points on single individuals, sometimes including cell phone data, credit card transactions, SSN, date of birth, and even [driving data](https://apnews.com/article/ftc-gm-driving-data-insurers-a555abb56a0d5f31afa9b73c3eb48287). There’s currently no comprehensive federal right for individuals to see, correct, or opt out of data being compiled about them. Think I’m exaggerating? I fact-checked this bullet with a few LLMs:  
​  
Claude Opus 4.5: “The claims check out. The piece is well-sourced on the data broker landscape.”  
​  
Gemini 3: “This text is a blend of accurate industry data, specific historical quotes, and a slightly outdated statistic that actually understates the current scale of the data broker industry.”  
​  
And this was all **before** AI. I’ll save quantum computing considerations for another time.
